But MEASURED ~20-32% SLOWER on shape5 (CLU 2/4/8 all 8.2-9.1ms vs single-CTA 6.85ms): the m-split is barrier-bound. ROOT CAUSE (intrinsic, not fixable by tuning): every trailing column's rank-1 update is preceded by a cross-stripe dot reduction = >=1 cl.sync()/column (~306ns each, ~2/col after I cut from 3), AND the m-split loses the single-CTA cm_coop_h kernel's look-ahead warp-specialization (bulk warps update trailing cols overlapped with the pivot critical path). This is DIFFERENT from your within-panel WMMA apply (that kept the linear chain + added tensor-core per step). Native (H,tau), no recon. Brief-4 (TSQR multi-CTA panel for n1024 underfill): PROTOTYPED THE MAKE-OR-BREAK FIRST exactly as the brief instructed -- and it decisively answers the brief's open question (does CTA-fill beat the combine cost at the underfilled shapes). THREE measured blockers: (1) BACK-TRANSFORM COST: emitting native (H,tau) from a Q,R requires the orhr_col recon, measured at 2568us for n1024 B60 = 81% of the ENTIRE current 3166us n1024 time. So even a FREE, perfectly-parallel K-CTA local-QR factor (the part TSQR's CTA-fill speeds up) cannot make TSQR win -- the back-transform alone is 81% of budget before any combine, and it is pure overhead on top of TSQR's own O(n^3) factor (TSQR does the QR work ~twice: factor + recon-to-standard-form). (2) BACK-TRANSFORM CORRECTNESS: the recon FAILS the n1024 orth gate (0.0254 vs 0.0122, even from a torch-EXACT Q,R; TF32-off no help) -- it is too imprecise for n1024's tight gate. (3) SQUARE MATRIX: the problem is n x n (m==n), but TSQR (Tall-Skinny QR) needs m>>n; a row-split of a square matrix gives WIDE (non-tall-skinny) blocks. TSQR only applies to the PANEL (tall-skinny m x IB), but a multi-CTA panel that emits NATIVE reflectors with NO per-column cross-CTA barrier is the cluster m-split = BARRIER-BOUND (brief-0 dead); the barrier-free independent-row-block form needs the per-panel recon (overhead). This is the FUNDAMENTAL DILEMMA, now fully measured across briefs 0+4: native-(H,tau) forces EITHER column-serial (per-column cross-CTA barrier OR 1-CTA underfill) OR a Q-producing method (TSQR/CholeskyQR) that needs the 81%-cost recon. Both horns blocked.
